title: From Predicates to Ranking Functions: LLM-Proposed, SMT-Certified Candidates for CEGAR-Based Software Verification
description:
Artifact for the Formal Methods final project report of the same title. VGuide augments CPAchecker with a large language model acting as a verified-candidate provider: the LLM proposes a candidate artifact (a loop predicate for safety, or a ranking function with a supporting invariant for termination), a sound SMT check certifies it, and only then is it used; no unvalidated LLM output can change a verdict (strictly Tier S).

This artifact bundles the VGuide source (a CPAchecker fork), configurations, benchmark lists, recorded experiment outputs, and evaluation scripts. The termination result (report Table 3: 80 -> 84 solved, +4, 0 lost, 0 wrong) regenerates deterministically and offline with python3 reproduce_termination.py (no API key, no solver, no CPAchecker run). The predicate results (Tables 1-2) are documented with their recorded run reports and can be re-run live. See README.md for Getting Started and Step-by-Step instructions.
notes: Reproduction artifact for the National Taiwan University Formal Methods (2026) final project report of the same title. Offline reproduction of the main termination result: run 'python3 reproduce_termination.py' (no API key, no network, no CPAchecker invocation). See README.md for Getting Started and Step-by-Step instructions. Built on CPAchecker (Apache-2.0).
method: VGuide intercepts CPAchecker at two points: (i) on the first spurious counterexample in predicate-CEGAR, an LLM proposes loop predicates that are filtered by a three-tier validation cascade (contract, scope-vocabulary, Z3 SMT entailment) before injection; and (ii) when lasso-based template synthesis fails for a loop, an LLM proposes a ranking function with an optional supporting invariant that is certified by four SMT checks (initiation, consecution, boundedness, decrease) before use. No unvalidated LLM output can change a verdict. Evaluation is on SV-COMP benchmarks with CPAchecker; the termination result is reproduced offline from recorded per-task outputs.
